transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Sarah Lopez (Cypress, Head of ML), Mark Rivera (Cypress, Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Cypress, CTO)

Summary:
- Goal: scope a 2-week pilot to validate cost model and performance for Cypress Dynamics' chat/assistant workloads.
- Key metrics: avg request length 220-300 tokens, 200 sustained qps target with 800 qps peak for certain events, monthly estimate ~50M raw tokens.
- Action: Redwood to send cost spreadsheet, run benchmark, share security docs.

Topics covered: success criteria, workload characterization, benchmarks to run, timeline for pilot, unit economics (per-token), batching and cache levers, budget constraints and fallbacks.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, this is Maya from Redwood, with Dev our SE. how's everyone doin?
[00:12] Sarah: hey, yes thanks — good. just a quick note, i might drop for five minutes later, back-to-back, but i'll be here.
[00:19] Dev: cool. quick agenda: we want to nail down success criteria, get workload sizing, and agree on what bench we'll run — and then map to cost implications.
[00:30] Priya: sounds good, high level we want to be sure we can meet latency SLOs (95p < 350ms for short convs) and keep monthly costs under 20k for initial pilot ideally.
[00:41] Maya: got it. when you say "monthly costs under 20k" is that for production scale or pilot?
[00:45] Priya: that's for pilot scale that we'd feel comfortable extrapolating from — we know production will be higher.
[00:52] Mark: just to frame, our current stack is a mix of cloud-hosted endpoints using OpenAI for prototypes and an internal cache layer; we pay about $0.0008-0.0012 per token right now on the prototype.
[01:07] Dev: ok. when you say current per-token, that's for hosted models? and which model size roughly?
[01:12] Mark: yeah hosted — mostly MPT-like and some GPT-3.5 equivalents, with about 50ms local latency plus network. not ideal.
[01:20] Sarah: our core workload is a document-assisted agent: user prompt ~60 tokens, doc context pulled ~180 tokens, output ~220 tokens avg. so round trip 460 tokens typical.
[01:35] Maya: that's super helpful. so per request avg 450-500 tokens. at 200 qps sustained that's... math.
[01:43] Dev: quick calc — 200 qps * 3600s * 24 * 30 = 518M requests/month? wait, no, sorry, that's wrong math, too many zeros — let's do it on calls/minutes. actually 200 qps * 3600 = 720k requests/hour, times 24 is 17.28M requests/day, times 30 is ~518M requests/month, yes that's right. but you said 50M tokens not requests — we need to be careful with tokens vs requests.
[02:10] Mark: yeah we expect only a subset of traffic to hit the assistant; our product analyst estimated 3M requests/month for pilot traffic, not 500M.
[02:18] Dev: ok that aligns: 3M requests * 480 tokens/request ≈ 1.44B tokens/month raw. so big numbers.
[02:30] Sarah: that seems high; our initial estimate of 50M tokens was after caching and truncation — real raw token volume is much larger.
[02:38] Maya: good catch. this is exactly why batching and KV-caching matter for unit economics — you can reduce token generation significantly.
[02:45] Priya: can you walk through the math and what knobs we have?
[02:49] Dev: sure. baseline per-token inference cost depends on model and quantization. rough numbers for Redwood hosted: 8-bit quantized Llama/Redwood-like medium models ≈ $0.00035 per token, fp16 large models closer to $0.0012 per token. those are ballpark and we'll put exact bands in the spreadsheet.
[03:12] Mark: those are lower than what we pay now, interesting. what's the tradeoff on quality?
[03:16] Dev: slight quality delta on edge cases; for many assistant tasks 8-bit quantized medium models are within acceptable thresholds. we also provide rollbacks to fp16 variants for canarying.
[03:26] Sarah: what about batching — how much does that save?
[03:29] Dev: batching reduces compute per-token by improving GPU utilization. for small responses it can reduce effective per-token cost by ~10-30% depending on qps and distribution. combined with prefix caching (we call it KV-ish cache), you can save an additional 20-60% on tokens if many requests reuse context.
[03:47] Maya: point being: raw token counts are scary; effective billable tokens after caching and dedup could be a fraction.
[03:53] Priya: ok, give me an example end-to-end for our 3M requests/month:
[03:58] Dev: sure — raw tokens: 3M * 480 ≈ 1.44B raw tokens. if caching + truncation reduces generated tokens by 70% (common for doc-retrieval scenarios where doc context is cached), you get ~432M effective tokens. if we also apply batching gains and model selection you might drop compute-equivalent further; assume per-token charge at $0.00035 gives $151k/month — which is above your 20k target. but with more aggressive caching, and a hybrid routing policy (small model for 80% traffic, fp16 for 20% only), you can get to ~ $30k-$40k.
[04:34] Mark: that's still above the pilot budget. how do others handle it?
[04:37] Maya: customers often start with a smaller sample (e.g., 300k requests/day) for pilot benchmarking and use targeted caching and aggressive truncation rules, plus model selection, to show a path to acceptable economics.
[04:50] Sarah: so our ask: can Redwood run a benchmark on our sample prompts and measure effective token usage after caching, and give a per-month extrapolation across a few scale scenarios?
[04:59] Dev: yes. we typically do: 1) run a 1-hour sustained run at 100 qps using your prompts, 2) enable caching + batching and measure token reduction and latency, 3) run a peak burst test. we'll capture 95/99p latency and actual billable token counts.
[05:15] Priya: timeline? we need results before Jan exec review (first week of Feb ideally).
[05:21] Maya: we can run the benchmark week of 2027-01-04 and deliver a spreadsheet plus a recorded run by 2027-01-12.
[05:28] Mark: good. security: we need to see SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS, and VPC options. also audit logs.
[05:36] Maya: we'll share those docs; Redwood Private options exist if we need customer-managed VPC or an on-prem pattern.
[05:41] Sarah: can you also show how Dedicated reserved capacity prices compare to hosted usage? sometimes committed capacity reduces unit cost a lot.
[05:50] Dev: yes, Dedicated commitment often reduces per-token cost by 20-40% depending on commit level and model. we'll include a few commitment bands in the spreadsheet.
[05:59] Priya: and fallback policies? if Dedicated capacity is saturated during peak we need auto-fallback to hosted to maintain availability.
[06:06] Dev: yup, smart routing supports fallbacks to compatible model variants in other regions or hosted pools — that's configurable.
[06:12] Mark: for benchmarking, do you need any infra changes on our side?
[06:16] Dev: just a small proxy to stream prompts, and sample dataset. we can provide a small harness — or you can run locally and we'll collect logs.
[06:24] Sarah: we can export 1k representative prompts and some doc chunks by tomorrow.
[06:29] Maya: perfect. we'll use that for the one-hour 100 qps run.
[06:33] Priya: on numbers, can you give a quick back-of-envelope: if we can get effective tokens down to 150M/month, what's monthly cost?
[06:41] Dev: at $0.00035/token that's $52.5k. at $0.0002/token (heavy quantization/commit) that's $30k. so still above your 20k target — you'd need either fewer requests or much higher cache reuse to get sub-20k at this scale.
[07:01] Mark: are there product knobs to lower tokens per request? like truncation, few-shot reduction?
[07:05] Dev: yes — truncate docs, use incremental retrieval, use cached embeddings for rerank to avoid re-sending huge contexts, and apply response length caps. also adjust system messages and move static context into metadata that doesn't count as billable if cached on the host side.
[07:20] Sarah: how precise are your per-token estimates? we need conservative and optimistic bands.
[07:24] Maya: we'll send bands; typical breakdown: optimistic (heavy caching + commitment) $0.00015-0.00025/token, base hosted quantized $0.0003-0.0005, large fp16 $0.0009-0.0015.
[07:38] Priya: fine, we just need to see the spreadsheet and the benchmark results.
[07:42] Dev: for the benchmark we'll measure: raw tokens in, effective generated tokens, 95/99p latency, GPU utilization, and per-token billing equivalent. we'll also test with small/medium model split to show routing economics.
[07:55] Maya: question for Cypress — what's your success criteria for the pilot beyond cost? for example tolerable latency, correctness delta thresholds, uptime, and what stakeholders sign off?
[08:06] Sarah: success = 1) 95p latency < 350ms for 80% of flows, 2) quality parity with internal baseline (<=5% drop on NLU eval sets), 3) demonstrable path to sub-$50k/month at scale with model/ops knobs, 4) security sign-off.
[08:24] Mark: and engineering readiness and ability to integrate routing and cache with our infra in 2-3 weeks.
[08:30] Dev: good, we'll codify those into the pilot SOW.
[08:34] Priya: about timeline, if we run bench week of Jan 4 and pilot starts Jan 10 for two weeks, we could have pilot data by end of Jan and an exec review in first week of Feb.
[08:46] Maya: yep that's feasible. we'll send the bench harness and the cost model spreadsheet by Dec 23 and schedule bench run early Jan.
[08:52] Sarah: any known gotchas — egress costs or hidden charges?
[08:56] Dev: not many hidden charges; network egress to your VPC is typical cloud egress. we'll show line items for compute, storage (KV cache), and egress in the spreadsheet. also note that streaming responses can slightly affect measured latency but not usually cost much.
[09:12] Mark: competitor question — how do you compare to Anthropic/Bedrock on cost?
[09:16] Maya: price bands are similar sometimes, but Redwood focuses on production predictability (dedicated pools, routing, and observability) which helps control unit economics. we'll include fair-market comps.
[09:27] Sarah: ok. anything else?
[09:29] Dev: one more technical note: sequence length greatly affects perf; if you can truncate to essentials and move long documents to retrieval, you save a lot.
[09:38] Maya: perfect. let's recap next steps.
[09:41] Priya: recap: bench + cost spreadsheet + security docs + pilot SOW.
[09:45] Maya: yes. we'll send spreadsheet by Dec 23 and target bench week Jan 4.
[09:50] Sarah: we'll share prompts today/tomorrow.
[09:53] Maya: great. thanks everyone.
[09:56] Mark: thanks.
[09:58] End of call.

Notes on transcription: some names and acronyms may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash in places), timestamps are approximate.
